bodyHtml:
Every prop firm account is a set of rules. Break one, and the account ends, however good your trading was. This chapter explains each rule type you will meet at the main U.S. futures firms, how the maths works, and how the same rule can behave differently from one firm to the next. It is the reference chapter for the rest of the track.

Numbers are quoted from each firm's help pages as of September 2026, for $50K accounts unless noted. Firms change them often, so always check the current page for your exact plan.

Key takeaways

  • The maximum loss limit (drawdown) is the rule that ends most accounts. Know whether yours is static, end-of-day trailing or intraday trailing, and where it stops trailing.
  • Intraday trailing counts open profit: giving back an unrealised gain moves your floor up for good.
  • Consistency rules cap how much of your profit can come from one day. They change the target, not just the payout.
  • Contract limits, close times, news rules and minimum days are all enforceable. Put every one in your trading plan.

The maximum loss limit

The maximum loss limit, also called max drawdown or trailing threshold, is the lowest balance your account may reach. Touch it and the account fails. Topstep's page puts it plainly: "If your balance hits it at any point during the trading day, including on unrealized P&L, your account is liquidated immediately."

There are three main designs.

Static

A static floor never moves. On a $50K account with a $2,000 limit, the floor is $48,000 for the life of the account. Many forex/CFD firms use a static overall limit (Blue Guardian's 2-Step lists 8% static, as of September 2026).

End-of-day (EOD) trailing

An EOD trailing floor moves up only when your account closes the day at a new high. Topstep's example: start at $50,000 with the limit at $48,000; make $500 on day 1 and the limit trails up to $48,500; lose $500 on day 2 and it stays at $48,500. Tradeify describes its version the same way: it "recalculates only at market close", but "the limit itself is still enforced in real time".

Intraday trailing

An intraday trailing floor follows the highest balance reached at any moment, including open profit. Apex's help page gives the example: a $50,000 evaluation with a $2,000 drawdown starts with the floor at $48,000. If open profit lifts the balance to $50,900, the floor jumps to $48,900 immediately, "No closing trade is required". If the trade then closes at $50,300, the floor stays at $48,900.

Look at day 4 in the chart. The account ran to $51,900 and closed at $51,100. Under the intraday rule the floor is now $49,900, leaving $1,200 of room. Under the EOD rule the floor stays at $49,400 (its best close is $51,400), leaving $1,700. Same trades, $500 less room, just because of the rule design. That is why intraday-trailing accounts reward taking profit and punish letting winners give back.

Where trailing stops

Most trailing floors stop rising at some level, which makes the account far safer from then on. This is one of the most important numbers on any plan page:

Topstep Trading Combine

Type: EOD trailing

Limit: $2,000

Where it stops trailing: Locks at the $50,000 starting balance

Apex Performance Account (intraday)

Type: Intraday trailing

Limit: $2,000

Where it stops trailing: Stops at $50,100 (start + $100)

Tradeify Growth

Type: EOD trailing

Limit: $2,000

Where it stops trailing: Locks at $50,100

MFFU Flex sim funded

Type: EOD trailing

Limit: $2,000

Where it stops trailing: Fixed at $100 after first payout

Apex, for example, says the intraday floor of a 50K Performance Account stops at $50,100 once the highest balance reaches $52,100 (start + $2,000 + $100). From that point on, the account can lose everything above $50,100 and survive. Until then, every new high tightens the rope.

Funded accounts that start at $0

Some firms show funded balances from zero. Topstep's Express Funded Account starts at $0 with the 50K limit at −$2,000; once the balance reaches $2,000 the limit locks at $0. After the first payout, Topstep sets the limit to $0 whatever it was before, so the remaining balance becomes your whole cushion. It is the same idea as a trailing floor, just drawn from a different starting point.

Daily loss limits

A daily loss limit (DLL) caps how much you can lose in one trading day. Firms treat it in two different ways, and the difference matters:

  • Soft stop: trading is paused until the next session, but the account survives. Topstep says triggering its DLL "is not a rule violation — it's a forced break", and Apex says hitting the DLL on its Performance Account "pauses trading for the remainder of the session".
  • Hard breach: the account fails. Many forex/CFD firms work this way; Blue Guardian's 2-Step, for example, breaches the account when the daily loss exceeds 4% of the initial balance.

Also check what the "day" is. Topstep's trading day runs 5:00 p.m. CT to 3:10 p.m. CT, so a trade at 6:30 p.m. Tuesday counts toward Wednesday. Tradeify warns that trading at 1:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on one calendar day can count as two trading days.

Consistency rules

A consistency rule limits how much of your total profit can come from your single best day. It is designed to stop one lucky day passing an evaluation or unlocking a payout.

Topstep's Trading Combine uses 55%: "Your single best day of profit must stay at or below 55% of your Profit Target. If it exceeds that, your Profit Target increases." On a 50K with a $3,000 target, that means a best day under $1,650.

Here is the effect, worked with Topstep's formula (best day ÷ total profit):

Best dayShare of $3,000Total profit needed
$1,60053%$3,000 (target unchanged)
$2,20073%$4,000 (so the best day is 55%)

A $2,200 day feels like progress, but it raises the bar to $4,000. Other firms use different numbers and apply them at different stages: LucidMaxx uses 40% in the evaluation; Apex's EOD Performance Account requires that no day be 50% or more of profit since the last payout; MFFU's Flex plan uses 50% in the evaluation only.

Position size, scaling and product rules

Every plan has a maximum position size. Topstep's 50K Combine allows 5 contracts or 50 micros, with micros counted at 10:1. Tradeify's 50K allows 4 minis or 40 micros. Funded accounts often add a scaling plan, where the limit rises with your balance: MFFU's Flex sim funded account allows 1 mini below $1,500 of profit, 2 up to $1,999, and 3 from $2,000.

Product rules vary too. Tradeify does not allow micros and minis to be held at the same time. Tradeify and Lucid prohibit hedging (opposite positions on the same or related contracts), including across accounts. Always read the approved products list, because some contracts aren't available at all.

Time rules

  • Close time: most futures firms are day-trade only. Tradeify requires all positions closed by 4:45 p.m. ET; Topstep's day ends at 3:10 p.m. CT.
  • Minimum days: Apex's current EOD and intraday evaluations list no minimum; Tradeify Growth lists 1 day and Select 3; MFFU lists 2; LucidMaxx lists 5. Topstep says you can pass "in as few as two days".
  • Inactivity: MFFU's Flex sim funded page lists a 7-calendar-day inactivity rule. Going quiet can close an account.
  • News: MFFU's news-restricted accounts must be flat from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after Tier 1 releases; Topstep prohibits trading your full maximum size into a scheduled major news event.

When the rules change

Firms update rules often, sometimes several times a year. Before you trade each week, check three things: the date on your plan's rule page, whether any announcement says the change applies to existing accounts or only new ones, and whether your rule card still matches. If a change is unclear, ask support in writing which version applies to your account, and keep the answer with your saved copy of the page (PF-03 covers keeping this paper trail).

Worked example: turning rules into a one-page card

Illustrative. Before your first trade on a new plan, write a rule card and keep it next to your chart:

RuleMy plan (example: EOD trailing 50K)
Loss floor todayBest close minus $2,000; stops at $50,100
Daily loss$1,000 soft stop (optional add-on)
ConsistencyBest day under 55% of target
Max size5 minis / 50 micros; one type at a time
Flat by3:10 p.m. CT; no full size into CPI/FOMC/NFP
Minimum days2

Update the loss floor line every evening. It is the one number that tells you how much room you really have tomorrow.

Common mistakes

Thinking the floor uses closed trades only

Better approach: Check whether your plan is intraday or EOD trailing. Intraday counts open profit.

Letting a big open winner come back

Better approach: On intraday trailing, take partial profit or move your stop, because the floor has already moved up.

Forgetting the consistency rule

Better approach: Set a daily profit cap near the limit; some platforms can enforce it.

Mixing up soft and hard daily limits

Better approach: Read whether hitting the DLL pauses or fails the account.

Trading into news on a restricted account

Better approach: Put the release times in your calendar with a two-minute buffer.

Practice exercises

  1. For your plan, write down the loss limit type, amount, and the balance at which it stops trailing.
  2. Using the eight-day path in this chapter, what would the intraday floor be after day 5? And the EOD floor?
  3. On a $3,000 target with a 55% consistency rule, what total profit do you need if your best day is $1,980?
  4. Build the one-page rule card for your plan and keep it next to your chart for a week.

Self-check quiz

1. What is the difference between EOD and intraday trailing drawdown?

EOD trails your best closing balance. Intraday trails your best balance at any moment, including open profit.

2. On Apex's 50K intraday Performance Account, where does the floor stop?

At $50,100, once the highest balance reaches $52,100.

3. Is Topstep's Daily Loss Limit a rule violation?

No. It flattens and pauses trading for the session; the account stays eligible.

4. Exercise: floors after day 5?

Intraday: $50,600 (peak $52,600 minus $2,000). EOD: $50,300 (best close $52,300 minus $2,000).

5. Exercise: best day $1,980, 55% rule, $3,000 target. Total needed?

$1,980 ÷ 0.55 = $3,600.
